I've been using this bait for Channel cats the last month or so and it works pretty well.

What you'll need:

  • A pack of the cheapest hotdogs you can find
  • A box of jello powder (I use Strawberry, but I've seen people use Grape)
  • Garlic powder
  • 1 gallon ziplock bag

Cut the dogs into thirds and dump into the ziplock bag. Make sure to get all those sweet juices from the hotdog pack too and dump it in with the dogs. Next, dump the jello packet in. Then add a healthy dose of the garlic powder. Seal the bag (MAKE SURE IT'S SEALED!!!). Shake the bag and mix everything about, making sure the dogs get nicely coated. That's it. You can fish with it right away or let it marinate overnight. It will stay good for a couple of weeks in the fridge as well.

As a warning, be sure to have a latex glove with you for hook application, unless you like getting your shit sticky and smelly.
Cheap and easy catfish bait that you can make in minutes
How do keep a hotdog on the hook when you cast?
The skin toughens up if you let them marinate for a few days. You can also cut up some pantyhose and bag the bait that way, same as with chicken livers.
I've done the P.H. thing before and got questionable results. I was thinking to slide the dog down the shank and then tying the line. Normally for c.c. I use live brim for bait.

I usually just slide through the hook and all the way up to my line, similar to how you'd hook a weightless soft plastic worm and I cast side-handed instead of overhead and they stay on more often than not.

As far as live bait, there's nothing better than shad/bluegill for cats, for sure. If I'm fishing smaller ponds with smaller cats, I'll catch a bluegill and cut him into thirds and they just eat that up too!

The best way is to use a baiting hook, you can fashion one from a hanger quite easily or even some haywire. put the hook through the Center of the hotdog and grasp your swivel (for a swivel hook) or if you purchased prelined hooks with the loop just utilize the loop before attaching it to a swivel hook. Also, size the hook and bait to the type of catfish and size you expect to catch. Circle hooks are my preference when catfishing as they set incredibly well. When river fishing look for a fast flowing portion of the river that has a strong bend, this is where you will find channel cats. I also use Strawberry, but I use koolaid packs. Also an amazing trick when river fishing for cats is to place grain (I use wheat) in a five gallon bucket (WITH A LID) about 1/4 full fill it with water place the lid on it without pressing it closed, put it in the sun for a couple of weeks. It will ferment and smell like you killed all of your neighbors and put them in a vat of acid. when ready to go fishing close the lid, as if you spill this amazing concoction there is no coming back. When you get to the area of the river you are interested in fishing go upstream and pour a good amount of this chum into the water. the catfish will smell it upstream and downstream and try to find where it is coming from. It really doesn't take that much, but if you plan to fish all day it is not a bad idea to pour a lot. Then go setup your fishing rigs and enjoy the bounty of your lazy fishing.
Trebble hooks work well for dogs/liver as well. Attach a snap swivel to the end of your leader, run the shaft through your bait, then snap the hook onto your swivel.
